title: Fundamentals of Software Testing
learning_outcomes: Explain what fundamentals of software testing contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: testing objectives.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Quality comes from several kinds of evidence: unit tests, integration tests, static analysis, coding standards, and repeatable CI. Tests should assert observable behavior and include important failure and boundary cases. In this lesson, focus on testing objectives; then compare it with unit tests. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use fundamentals of software testing when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: PHP quality pipeline
content_blocks.alt_text: Small unit tests, integration tests, static analysis, and style checks provide different evidence.
content_blocks.caption: No single check proves quality

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Quality comes from several kinds of evidence: unit tests, integration tests, static analysis, coding standards, and repeatable CI. Tests should assert observable behavior and include important failure and boundary cases. For fundamentals of software testing, begin with testing objectives. Also distinguish unit tests; integration tests; functional tests. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Testing objectives
items.text: Write an assertion about observable behavior and include a boundary or failure case; a passing command alone does not prove the requirement.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Fundamentals of Software Testing
content_blocks.code:
<?php
function add(int $a, int $b): int { return $a + $b; }
$actual = add(2, 3);
echo $actual === 5 ? "PASS" : "FAIL";

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Test observable behavior, include boundary cases, and treat static analysis and coverage as evidence rather than proof.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for fundamentals of software testing from top to bottom. Start by identifying testing objectives, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

content.task: Create a second small example for fundamentals of software testing that demonstrates "testing objectives". Before running it, write down the expected result and one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of testing objectives.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary inputs and failures can reveal defects that normal examples miss.
common_mistakes.fix: Add empty, invalid, boundary, and failure cases with meaningful assertions.

common_mistakes.why: Tests can become brittle and stop checking real behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Prefer simple unit tests and focused integration tests at actual boundaries.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating coverage as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Executing a line does not guarantee its behavior was asserted.
common_mistakes.fix: Review assertions, relevant branches, edge cases, and regression risk.

summary: Fundamentals of Software Testing is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Test observable behavior, include boundary cases, and treat static analysis and coverage as evidence rather than proof.
